findings.result_name: The rotor game needs exponentially many chips (thm:fresh19-chips)
findings.defect: The theorem is FALSE as quantified: it asserts, for every m >= 1, that M_rho(n) > n/2 for every n < 7(2^m - 1), and at m = 1 the value of the rotor game equals n/2 at n = 2, 4 and 6, all of which are below the bound 7. The proof step 'for n <= 7 the schedule sending the i-th chip to u_i gives OUT_n = n' is false whenever 2^m - 1 < 7, i.e. for m = 1 and m = 2 (the q-chain is a rotor-router counter whose first chip to reach t0 is chip 2^m). The parity branch of the proof (n >= 7) is correct and the asymptotic content survives; the repair is to restrict the statement to m >= 3.
findings.evidence: RC(1) built from the STATEMENT (7 Max tree vertices 0..6 with children 2i+1,2i+2; 8 average leaves 7..14 each -> (15,t0); chain vertex 15 -> (t1,t0)); N = 18, mycore.is_stopping true, brute-force max-min val(v0) = 1/4 = 1/2 - 2^{-2}. Exact backward induction over (chips remaining, position, rotor configuration) in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/c506180a-e393-4ffa-a18f-efc78c98397e/scratchpad/r19-audit-fresh-19-correctness/aud_rotor.py, rho == 0, gives M_rho(n) = 1,1,2,2,3,3,4 for n = 1..7. So M_rho(2) = 1 = 2/2, M_rho(4) = 2 = 4/2, M_rho(6) = 3 = 6/2 -- the claimed strict inequality fails at three values of n below the bound. (Reason: after chip 1 the chain rotor at q_1 points at t0, and every leaf either sends the chip to q_1 or straight to t0, so chip 2 cannot reach t1 under ANY Max play.) At m = 2 the theorem's conclusion does hold (checked for all n < 21) but the quoted proof step fails there too: the schedule gives OUT_4 = 3, not 4. For m = 3,4,5,6 everything the route reports reproduces exactly: first failure of 2*OUT_n > n at n = 56,120,248,504 = 8*2^m - 8, minimum excess over n >= 7 exactly (7/2)val(q_1) = 49/16, 105/32, 217/64, 441/128, A/2 = 35/8, 75/16, 155/32 at m = 3,4,5. Script t5_rc.py, t12_rc_small.py, t13_rc1_exact.py.

findings.result_name: Bounded routing count collapses into the few-denominator class (prop:fresh19-collapse)
findings.defect: The statement's first clause -- 'Every value of every pair, hence every letter of Lambda(G), has denominator dividing nu(G)' -- is FALSE. What the routing formula gives is that the denominator divides |R(sigma,tau)| for that pair's OWN routing count; nu(G) is the MAXIMUM over pairs, and divisibility does not follow from an inequality. The conclusion of the proposition nevertheless survives, because val = val_{sigma*,tau*} for an optimal pair of a stopping game, so D(G) divides |R(sigma*,tau*)| <= nu(G), whence D(G) <= nu(G) and the class {nu <= q(N)} is inside thm:few-denominator with cost O(N^2 nu^2); only the stated divisibility must be replaced by that argument.
findings.evidence: Six-vertex stopping counterexample found by exhaustive search over random stopping games (t3b.py): kinds ['avg','max','avg','avg'], succ [(5,3),(0,4),(1,1),(2,4)] with t0 = 4, t1 = 5. The two pairs have routing counts 6 (sigma(1) = 0, the optimal one; two of the eight selections cycle 0->3->2->1->0) and 8 (sigma(1) = t0, acyclic), so nu(G) = 8; val = (2/3, 2/3, 2/3, 1/3), so D(G) = 3 and 3 does not divide 8. Both clauses of the sentence fail on this one instance. A second, independent sweep (t3_nudiv.py) found further counterexamples for the per-pair clause, e.g. a 6-non-sink game with nu = 8 and a pair with |R| = 7 whose value at v0 is 1/7. 19 of 1072 random stopping games had D(G) not dividing nu(G).

findings.result_name: The routing count is a common denominator, and equals a determinant (cor:fresh19-den)
findings.defect: GAP: the statement asserts 'det A_U divides |R| and is in general strictly smaller', but the argument section proves only det M = |R| and says nothing about det A_U; the divisibility is asserted, not proved. (It is true: contracting the deterministic rows of M leaves the matrix A on Vavg with det A = det M, and A is block triangular with respect to the splitting Vavg = U u (Vavg \ U) because from a vertex off U no successor reaches t1, so det A_U divides det A = |R|; three lines that the route does not supply.)
findings.evidence: I rebuilt A_U from the proof of lem:denominator (frontier.tex l.1179-1225: the D-contraction, mu_u(w) in {0,1,2}, restriction to the average vertices from which t1 is reachable) in t8_detAU.py: over 428 absorbing pairs of random games det A_U divides |R| in 428/428 and equals it in 334/428, consistent with the route's 253/253 and 192/253. So the clause is true but unproved as written.

findings.defect: GAP: 'the value M_rho(n) exists' is asserted with only 'the game is finite by lem-terminate'; the missing sentence is that finite branching plus the absence of infinite plays makes the reachable state graph on (chips remaining, position, rotor configuration) a finite DAG, so backward induction assigns a value -- otherwise determinacy of the rotor game is a fifth import.
findings.evidence: The route's fresh19:lem-terminate proves only that every play is finite. My own solver (aud_rotor.chip_game_value) had to add an explicit on-path cycle check to justify the recursion; it never fired on any of the 600 random stopping games or on E1, RC(1), RC(2), RC(3), which confirms the DAG property but is exactly the step the write-up omits.

findings.defect: GAP: the theorem is stated for an arbitrary absorbing pair, but its proof invokes fresh19:lem-terminate, which is stated and proved only for a STOPPING SSG; the absorbing-pair version of termination (the infinitely-visited set is closed for the pair chain, hence never reaches a sink) is used without being stated.
findings.evidence: fresh19:lem-terminate in the route's LaTeX reads 'On a stopping SSG every play of ROT_rho(n) is finite', and its proof ends by contradicting lem:trapchar, a statement about the game. thm-period's proof: 'Phi is well defined by lem-terminate'. My t7_period.py had to prove termination for the pair chain separately; the theorem's conclusion reproduced on 1503 (game, pair, rotor start) instances (OUT_p/p = val exactly, every K_u even, p <= 2^a, and the route's declared GAP p | |R| held in all 1503).

findings.result_name: The behavioural value is a ratio of multilinear forms (prop:fresh19-mixed, clause 2)
findings.defect: The retyping clause describes Z^0, Z^1 as 'the numbers Z^i of routings with f(v) = i'. That is a count only when the other controlled coordinates are frozen at pure values; for a general p in [0,1]^C, which is the setting of the proposition, Z^i = B(p with p_v = i) is a p-WEIGHTED sum of routing counts, not a number of routings, and the phrase 'the routing-count-weighted convex combination' is then wrong as stated.
findings.evidence: Verified in t9_mixed.py: with the other controlled vertices frozen at pure 0/1 the identity val = (Z^0 v^0 + Z^1 v^1)/(Z^0 + Z^1) with Z^i literal routing counts holds on 150/150 random stopping games; the general-p version holds only with Z^i read as B(p|p_v=i), which is a weighted sum. (The route's own verification used pure freezings, so the computation matches the weaker reading, not the stated one.)

findings.result_name: Bounded routing count collapses into the few-denominator class (prop:fresh19-collapse)
findings.defect: Miscitation and overreach: the class is said to be 'solved in O(N^2 nu(G)^2) by thm:alphabet-iteration', but thm:alphabet-iteration is the exactness of the rounded iteration on a grid; the algorithm that needs no advance knowledge of D and costs O(N^2 D(G)^2) is thm:few-denominator. And the closing sentence 'No polynomial class outside the eight known ones arises from a bound on the number of routings' is broader than what is proved, which is only that {G stopping : nu(G) <= q(N)} lies inside thm:few-denominator.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.2782-2802 (thm:few-denominator: 'For D = 1,2,3,... run cor:grid-iteration ... The cost is sum_{D <= D(G)} O(N^2 D) = O(N^2 D(G)^2)') against l.2561 (thm:alphabet-iteration), which states exactness on a grid containing the values and carries no such cost bound.

findings.result_name: The routing count is a common denominator, and equals a determinant (cor:fresh19-den)
findings.defect: In the base case a = 0 the cyclic branch is argued by saying the cycle's rows 'form I minus a cyclic permutation, so det M = 0'; that identifies a singular principal submatrix, which does not by itself give det M = 0. The direct reason -- the rows indexed by the cycle sum to the zero vector, so M is singular -- is one line and is not the one given.
findings.evidence: Route LaTeX, proof of fresh19:cor-den. The conclusion is correct: det M = |R| verified with 0 mismatches on 7840 pairs from 600 random games (t1_formula.py) and 14117 pairs from 1500 games engineered with duplicated successors and self-loops (t11_misc.py).

findings.result_name: The rotor game needs exponentially many chips (thm:fresh19-chips)
findings.defect: RC(m) holds |Vmax| = 7 and the number of average leaves = 8 constant while only the chain length m grows, and |Vmin| = 0, so the family is one-player and lies inside thm:one-player / the trivial min(m,k) = O(log N) class; the theorem therefore bounds the CHIP READOUT, not the difficulty of the instances. This is what the statement says, but the family should not be read as evidence about prob:main, and the chip bound 7(2^m - 1) is of the same order as the trivial ceiling 2^a = 2^{m+8} on the rotor period (thm:fresh19-period).
findings.evidence: RC(m) built from the statement: 7 Max, 8 + m average, 0 Min, a = m + 8, N = m + 17; every vertex reachable from v0 (so no unreachable-vertex artefact). mycore.is_stopping true for m = 1..6.

verdict: Two majors survive, so the route is NOT sound as submitted, but the damage is local and repairable: the mathematics of the routing formula and of the rotor identity is correct, and I reproduced every other numerical claim independently. WHAT I CHECKED AND WHAT HELD. (1) The routing formula and the nonemptiness lemma: I reconstructed both proofs line by line -- the term-by-term matching A^0 + A^1 = W_1 + W_2 at an average vertex is correct, including the degenerate cases u^(0) = u and u^(0) = u^(1), and the attractor/closed-set argument is correct -- and verified them on 7840 pairs from 600 random games on 2-7 non-sinks, on G8, S, S_r(4), H_m(4), G_m(5) and the non-stopping A0, and on 14117 pairs from 1500 games engineered to have duplicated successors and self-loops: 0 violations anywhere. (2) det M = |R| on the same sweeps (0 mismatches) and, without enumeration, on the three large published games: every pair's value denominator divides det M on B2_small (N = 138, 64 pairs), H11_m5 (N = 260, 32 pairs) and B1 (N = 58, 8 pairs), with log2 det M in [120.7, 128.5], [243.2, 252.5], [47.6, 52.5] -- consistent with the route's 127, 247, 51. The induction (linearity of the determinant in the average row, matched with |R| = |R^0| + |R^1|) is correct. (3) The characterisation |R| = 2^a iff the pair digraph is acyclic: 0 failures. (4) The rotor identity: the telescoping and the pairwise cancellation of consecutive visits are correct; verified exactly on 288 random (game, play, rotor start, n). (5) The sandwich: the proof is correct (Max's terms vanish on an optimal successor, Min's are nonnegative, the rotor deviation is at least -A/2), and I confirmed it against 600 exact chip-game values computed by my own backward induction over (chips remaining, position, rotor configuration); on E1 the constant is attained at BOTH ends -- M_(0,0)(n) = n/2 + 1 and M_(1,1)(n) = n/2 - 1 for even n -- and the best SSG-positional Max forces exactly ceil(n/2), so the lossiness claim reproduces. The HEADLINE is therefore a sentence the route proved. (6) The period theorem on 1503 (game, pair, rotor) instances, with the declared GAP (period divides |R|) holding in all of them -- I found no refutation. (7) The biased multilinear proposition and the retyping identity, 150 instances each on the grid of sixths, 0 mismatches. WHAT BROKE. thm:fresh19-chips is false at m = 1: exact backward induction on RC(1) gives M_rho(2) = 1, M_rho(4) = 2, M_rho(6) = 3, i.e. exactly n/2 and not more, at three values of n below the claimed bound 7(2^1 - 1) = 7; the proof step 'for n <= 7 the schedule gives OUT_n = n' is false for every m <= 2 because the q-chain is a rotor-router counter whose 2^m-th chip is the first to reach t0. Restricting to m >= 3 repairs statement and proof, and the 2^{Omega(N)} content and all measured rows (m = 3,4,5,6) reproduce exactly. And prop:fresh19-collapse's clause 'every value of every pair, hence every letter of Lambda(G), has denominator dividing nu(G)' is false -- a six-vertex stopping game with nu = 8, an optimal pair of routing count 6 and D(G) = 3 kills it -- although the collapse itself stands through D(G) | |R(sigma*,tau*)| <= nu(G). Four minor gaps (det A_U | |R| asserted without proof, though true and provable in three lines by block triangularity; the existence of the rotor game's value; the absorbing-pair form of termination used by the period theorem; the count-vs-weight reading of Z^i at general p) and one miscitation (thm:alphabet-iteration for thm:few-denominator's cost bound). I found no instance of the project's standing errors: no greedy policy iteration, no dict-literal row collapse (I accumulate everywhere and so does the route's core), sinks carried as indices n, n+1 with no collision, traps computed as closed sets admitting t0, no stall claimed anywhere so the three readings of the standing rule do not apply, no unreachable vertex used to separate a family, no non-dyadic witness, and every family member -- E1, RC(1), RC(2), RC(3), RC(4), RC(5), RC(6) -- assembled as a game by me and measured from the game. I started no background jobs; the python3 processes on the box belong to other round-19 routes.
